# omniddi_dns_record (Resource)

Manages a DNS record set (one owner name and type) in an OmniDDI zone. One resource covers every record type OmniDDI accepts; pick the value form that matches `type`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omniddi_dns_zone" "corp" {
  name      = "corp.example.com"
  view_name = "internal"
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "www"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  values  = ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.11"]
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "www_v6" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "www"
  type    = "AAAA"
  values  = ["2001:db8::10"]
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "delegation" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "lab"
  type    = "NS"
  values  = ["ns1.lab.corp.example.com.", "ns2.lab.corp.example.com."]
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "sip" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "_sip._tcp"
  type    = "SRV"

  srv {
    priority = 10
    weight   = 60
    port     = 5060
    host     = "sip1.corp.example.com"
  }

  srv {
    priority = 10
    weight   = 40
    port     = 5060
    host     = "sip2.corp.example.com"
  }
}

data "omniddi_dns_zone" "reverse" {
  name      = "2.0.192.in-addr.arpa"
  view_name = "internal"
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "www_ptr" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.reverse.id
  name    = "10"
  type    = "PTR"
  values  = ["www.corp.example.com."]
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "apex_mx" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "@"
  type    = "MX"

  mx {
    preference = 10
    exchange   = "mail1.example.com"
  }

  mx {
    preference = 20
    exchange   = "mail2.example.com"
  }
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "apex_caa" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "@"
  type    = "CAA"

  caa {
    flag  = 0
    tag   = "issue"
    value = "letsencrypt.org"
  }

  caa {
    flag  = 0
    tag   = "iodef"
    value = "mailto:security@example.com"
  }
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "verification" {
  zone_id         = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name            = "_verify"
  type            = "TXT"
  values          = ["token-current", "token-retiring"]
  disabled_values = ["token-retiring"]
}

resource "omniddi_dns_record" "service_binding" {
  zone_id = data.omniddi_dns_zone.corp.id
  name    = "svc"
  type    = "SVCB"

  data_json = jsonencode({
    priority = 1
    host     = "svc.example.com"
    alpn     = "h2"
    port     = 8443
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Owner name relative to the zone, for example `www`. Use `@` for the zone apex. Names are lower-cased by OmniDDI and compared case-insensitively. A trailing dot is significant: `www.` is an absolute name, `www` is relative to the zone.
- `type` (String) Record type, in upper case. One of: A, AAAA, ANAME, AFSDB, CAA, CNAME, DNAME, DNSKEY, DS, EUI48, EUI64, HINFO, HTTPS, ISDN, LOC, MB, MD, MF, MG, MR, MX, NAPTR, NS, PTR, PX, RP, RRSIG, RT, SOA, SPF, SRV, SSHFP, SVCB, TLSA, TXT, URI, X25. The value form depends on the type: `values` for string-shaped types (A, AAAA, NS, PTR, TXT, SPF, CNAME, DNAME, MB, MD, MF, MG, MR, SOA, DNSKEY, RRSIG, LOC, X25, EUI48, EUI64), the `mx`, `srv` or `caa` blocks for MX, SRV and CAA, and `data_json` for every other type (and optionally for MX, SRV and CAA). Changing it replaces the record.
- `zone_id` (Number) ID of the zone the record belongs to (`omniddi_dns_zone.id`). Changing it replaces the record.

### Optional

- `approval_mode` (String) How to behave when OmniDDI requires change approval: `fail` returns an error carrying the request id, `wait` waits until the request is applied. Defaults to the provider `approval_mode`.
- `caa` (Block List) CAA entries. A list because one name commonly carries both `issue` and `iodef`. Only for `type = "CAA"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--caa))
- `data_json` (String) Escape hatch: the record data as a JSON document, sent to OmniDDI as the record `data` payload. Required for AFSDB, ANAME, DS, HINFO, HTTPS, ISDN, NAPTR, PX, RP, RT, SSHFP, SVCB, TLSA and URI; optional for MX, SRV and CAA. Use `jsonencode`. Key order and whitespace are ignored when comparing. Object-shaped payloads (for example SVCB) are merged into the stored object by OmniDDI on update, so a removed key is not deleted. Numeric TLSA/SSHFP/DS fields are stored as integers.
- `disabled_values` (Set of String) Subset of `values` that stay in OmniDDI but are withheld from DNS answers. Only supported for A, AAAA, NS, PTR, TXT and SPF, and at least one value must remain enabled.
- `mx` (Block List) MX exchanges. Repeat the block for several exchanges. Only for `type = "MX"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--mx))
- `record_set_ordering` (String) Answer ordering for multi-value record sets: `default`, `random` or `cyclic`. OmniDDI only persists it for records with a load-balancing health check, which this provider does not manage yet, so the configured value is kept in state without being read back.
- `srv` (Block List) SRV targets. Repeat the block for several targets. Only for `type = "SRV"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--srv))
- `tags` (Map of String) Single-valued OmniDDI tags. Tag definitions must already exist. Merged with provider `default_tags`.
- `tags_list` (Map of List of String) Multi-valued (list) OmniDDI tags. Tag definitions must already exist.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `ttl` (Number) Record TTL in seconds. When omitted at creation OmniDDI stores the zone TTL. Removing the attribute later keeps the stored value; set it explicitly to change it.
- `values` (List of String) Values for string-shaped record types: A, AAAA, NS, PTR, TXT and SPF accept one or more values; CNAME, DNAME, MB, MD, MF, MG, MR, SOA, DNSKEY, RRSIG, LOC, X25, EUI48 and EUI64 take exactly one. Each TXT/SPF element is one value of the record set. Exactly one of `values`, `mx`, `srv`, `caa` or `data_json` must be set, and it must match `type`.

### Read-Only

- `created_on` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `effective_ttl` (Number) TTL in effect: the record TTL, or the zone TTL when the record has none.
- `id` (Number) The OmniDDI record ID.
- `is_auto_created` (Boolean) True for records created automatically during zone synchronisation. OmniDDI refuses to delete these and to toggle their values.
- `tags_all` (Map of String) All single-valued tags on the object, including those inherited from provider `default_tags`.
- `updated_on` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `view_id` (Number) ID of the DNS view that contains the zone.
- `zone_name` (String) Name of the zone the record belongs to.

<a id="nestedblock--caa"></a>
### Nested Schema for `caa`

Required:

- `flag` (Number) Issuer critical flag: `0` or `128`.
- `tag` (String) Property tag: `issue`, `issuewild` or `iodef`.
- `value` (String) Property value, for example `letsencrypt.org`.


<a id="nestedblock--mx"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mx`

Required:

- `exchange` (String) Mail exchanger host name.
- `preference` (Number) Preference (0-65535); lower is preferred.


<a id="nestedblock--srv"></a>
### Nested Schema for `srv`

Required:

- `host` (String) Target host name.
- `port` (Number) TCP/UDP port (0-65535).
- `priority` (Number) Priority (0-65535); lower is preferred.
- `weight` (Number) Relative weight (0-65535) among targets of equal priority.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import omniddi_dns_record.www 5021
terraform import omniddi_dns_record.www internal/corp.example.com/www/A
terraform import omniddi_dns_record.apex_mx 'internal/corp.example.com/@/MX'
```
